title: Payment API latency spike
executive_summary: Checkout latency (3-5s) and 5xx payment failures began at 14:00Z. payment-service's DB connection pool saturated (100% utilisation) because connections were leaked on the partial-refund path. Log pattern logpat-payment-service-9d1f3d29 shows 9 leak-detection warnings from RefundService.processPartialRefund (held >30s) starting 13:45Z, and pool timeouts (logpat-payment-service-7d1739af, 29 events) from 14:00Z. api-gateway latency and errors follow payment-service, consistent with downstream impact. Postgres and auth-service are healthy. No config change was found; the only deployment in the window (notification-service 3.4.1 at 13:54Z) has no link to the payment pool. Recommended immediate action: restart payment-service pods to release leaked connections, and roll back or fix the refund code path.

hypotheses.description: Connection leak in RefundService.processPartialRefund exhausts payment-db-pool in payment-service, causing acquisition timeouts, latency and 5xx that propagate to api-gateway. Mechanism: Refund path acquires pooled DB connections and does not release them (likely missing try-with-resources or a long-held transaction). Leaked connections accumulate from ~13:45Z, active reaches the 50-connection cap, and new checkout requests wait the full 5s acquisition timeout and fail. The retry and timeout path raises p95 and error rate.

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): db_connection_pool_exhaustion in payment-service - Connection leak in RefundService.processPartialRefund exhausts payment-db-pool in payment-service, causing acquisition timeouts, latency and 5xx that propagate to api-gateway.
corrective_actions: Restart payment-service pods to release leaked connections and restore checkout (immediate mitigation)
Fix the connection leak in RefundService.processPartialRefund: release connections in a finally block or try-with-resources, and bound transaction duration
Roll back any recent RefundService change if the leak is traced to a specific release
preventive_actions: Add a code review and integration test for connection release on exception paths in refund flows
Set a pool max-lifetime and a statement or transaction timeout for payment-db-pool
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on HikariPool connection-leak warnings (any occurrence) and on pool utilisation above 80% for 5 minutes
Track active connections held per call site (RefundService vs checkout) in payment-service
Dashboard payment-service timeout_rate and error_rate with pool wait time
limitations: Evidence is temporal and log-based; the leak was not reproduced
Trigger for the leak is not identified
Historical match similarity is only 0.35 and serves as an analogy only

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The payment-service latency spike and 5xx errors are caused by exhaustion of the payment-db-pool connection pool. Connections checked out by RefundService.processPartialRefund were leaked and held for more than 30s, so the pool filled (active=50, idle=0, large waiting queue) and new requests timed out acquiring connections. The database itself is not the bottleneck (postgres p95 latency flat at ~12ms, CPU and disk flat). The leak started at about 13:45Z, pool utilisation rose from 13:49Z, and saturation coincided with the 14:00Z onset of latency and errors. The mechanism matches a known historical pattern, but the trigger for the leak (code change or refund traffic change) is not yet confirmed.
